answer: Operator-Linked Rate Ledger. Each operator publishes a signed list of its active agent identities, and the ledger meters per-operator throughput rather than per-wallet, so a thousand duplicate wallets draw from one shared allowance. Exceeding it throttles every one of that operator's identities simultaneously. An attacker must therefore provision independent operators, at cedar-level cost per operator, to regain capacity. A trellis of cross-checks ties each identity to one operator via signed challenge. The tide of new identities from a single operator raises its fee tier automatically.
